technology: Titan (stack transcribed from the semantic sidecar via layer names)
_comment: The vertical connection stack is the one thing a .gds and a .lyp cannot tell you:
GDSII stores no layer elevations, and a .lyp stores colours and names. This file
supplies it explicitly, so the net graph is built from a stated stack rather than
These values are transcribed from the via layer names in the JSON sidecars, which
name each via after its two endpoints (VIA_M0_M1, VIA_M0_PMOSGate,
VIA_Inteconnect_BSPowerRail). The layer numbers agree with the .lyp, so the two
sources cross-check. They have still not been checked against a real Titan PDK.
Two corrections the sidecar names forced, both of which the .lyp names alone got
1. NDIFFCON / PDIFFCON are named NMOSInterconnect / PMOSInterconnect in the
sidecar. They are local interconnect CONDUCTORS, not contacts. Treating them
as contacts bridging diffusion to M0 shorted a whole cell into one net.
2. N-VIAT / P-VIAT land on those interconnect layers, not on the diffusion
This technology uses backside power delivery (the .lyp contains BSPDN-PMOS-VIA),
so BM0 is backside metal reached through DVB, not through the frontside vias that
merely overlap it in plan view.
_roles_comment: Corrects the role heuristic, which reads a name ending in CON as a contact.
Only layers whose inferred role is wrong need listing.
_same_level_comment: A gate crossing both wells is drawn as NPOLY over one and PPOLY over the other;
the two abut edge-to-edge and form one continuous conductor. Without this, an
NPOLY gate finger with no via of its own is reported as floating when it is in
fact part of a PPOLY net. Measured in NR2D1: NPOLY and PPOLY touch at 2 places
with zero overlap area, i.e. they meet edge-to-edge rather than stacking.
